mechanisms.name: tool-registry-and-scoped-visibility
mechanisms.what: `ToolRuntime` (Cordis Service at `ctx.tools`, `static inject = ['systemPrompt']`) is the single registry: `register()` inserts a `ToolDefinition` into a scoped `ToolLayer`, `restrict()` appends a compiled allow/deny filter, `guard()` appends a monotonic guard, and `view(scope)` derives one `ToolView { visible, knownNames, restrictableNames }` per scope in a single layer traversal. Restrictions filter only the INHERITED surface (the global layer plus ancestor layers), never the scope's own registrations, and the reserved `run_code` transport is appended last, outside capability filtering, only for scopes whose mode presents it. Scoped registrations shadow inherited ones by name; a duplicate name inside one layer, the reserved name, an empty/no-op restriction and a restriction naming an unknown or reserved tool all throw at registration time. `schemas(scope)` projects visible definitions onto only name/description/parameters, so `execute`, `output`, `timeoutMs` and `isConcurrencySafe` are never model-visible, and `executionMode()` classifies overlap fail-closed.
invariants: `register()` rejects the reserved PTC name `run_code` unconditionally, so a name free under the deployment default can never collide once a preset mounts a code mode (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1044-1046).
A restriction filters what a scope INHERITS (global plus ancestor layers) and never what its own layer registers (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1127-1138).

`executionMode()` is fail-closed: only an exact `true` from `isConcurrencySafe` is parallel; unknown, hidden, undeclared, invalid or throwing classifiers are exclusive (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1266-1275).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — duplicate/scoped-conflict/reserved-name/unknown-restriction-target all throw at registration; an invisible tool or a `ptc`-collapsed model-direct call resolves to `undefined` and materializes as an `UNKNOWN_TOOL` error result.
constants: reserved transport name `run_code` (packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:20; rejected at packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1044-1046)
`maxParallelSubCalls` config default 10, `z.natural().min(1)`, re-validated by `resolveMaxParallelSubCalls` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:660-666, 768-774, 785)
no cap on registered-tool count or restriction-entry count

mechanisms.name: tool-schema-dsl-and-output-contract
mechanisms.what: Tools declare arguments and results in an author-facing DSL (`defineTool({ parameters, output })`) that `schema.ts` compiles to the enforced raw JSON Schema subset of `json-schema.ts` through a stack-safe task graph (`runSchemaCompiler`), rejecting author-only keys, `type` together with `oneOf`, a missing `additionalProperties` on an object node and circular property maps. Every successful body value is snapshotted to lossless JSON, validated against `output.schema` inside `createSuccessResult`, deep-frozen and projected through the pure `output.render` (plus `presentationMeta` for top-level calls only). `defineTool` re-validates arguments at execute time (`ToolArgsError`, code `INVALID_ARGS`), while `presentCall`/`presentResult`/`isConcurrencySafe` validate softly and fall back to `undefined`/`false` so a replay of obsolete logged arguments can never throw.
invariants: Objects must state openness explicitly: `additionalProperties` must be present and boolean, so a nested or output object never acquires an accidental JSON Schema default (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:365-369).

The registry snapshots `finalizeContent` when the call starts and invokes it exactly once for every normalized outcome, including pipeline failures that bypass `tools/post-execute` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:228-239, 1388-1400).
`presentCall`/`presentResult` must never throw: a UI may call them during live streaming AND during session-log replay (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:594-609).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — author/schema errors and argument violations fail closed (throw at define/execute time); a value that is not lossless JSON or violates `output.schema` fails closed as `ToolOutputError` (code `INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT`); a throwing `render`/`presentationMeta` projector is converted into that same canonical invalid-output error instead of escaping.
constants: enforced keyword subset: type/oneOf/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const plus description/title/default/examples (packages/core/tools/src/json-schema.ts:76-87)
`oneOf` requires at least two branches (packages/core/tools/src/json-schema.ts:292-293)
type inference bounded to 16 container levels before falling back to `JsonValue` (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:154)
`defineTool` rejects `timeoutMs` that is non-finite or <= 0 (packages/core/tools/src/schema.ts:563-565)

mechanisms.name: tool-execution-pipeline-and-guards
mechanisms.what: One call traverses `tools/pre-execute` (waterfall returning `PreToolDecision` allow/deny/ask), then monotonic guards, then `tools/execute` (around-dispatch waterfall), then the tool body, then `tools/post-execute` (accept/replace/block), then the definition-owned `finalizeContent`, then lossless materialization and finally the `tools/result` emit. The ordered stages are exposed to the loop as a symbol-keyed `ToolRuntimeScheduler` (`prepare`/`dispatch`/`finalize`/`finish`, `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER`) so policy stays model-ordered while only the body overlaps. Guards registered through `tools.guard()` have no allow result, so listener ordering can never turn a denial back into permission; an `ask` decision resolves through the optional `approval` seam and degrades to denial when the seam or the agent is absent. The package's own invariant companion (`tools-invariant`) fails when a stage repeats, when `execute` does not follow `pre-execute`, or when the published `tools/result` execution/outcome is not frozen.
invariants: A guard can only deny; no guard can force-allow a call another guard denied (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:696-704, 1108-1118).
A collapsed (`ptc`) or unknown call must never reach `pre-execute`, an approval `ask`, or guards (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1363-1371).

`tools/result` observers receive a frozen execution and a frozen, lossless-JSON outcome; listener failures are contained and only logged (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1646-1666; packages/core/tools/src/invariant.ts:22-30).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — authorization is fail-closed (deny, ask-without-channel and a guard reason each materialize an `isError` result) and observers are fail-soft (a throwing `tools/result` listener is logged, a throwing waterfall listener turns the call into an `isError` result rather than rejecting the caller).
constants: `TOOL_ABORTED` = 'ABORTED' and `TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` = 'ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH' are the two canonical cancellation codes (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:462-465)
`ToolNotFoundError` carries code `UNKNOWN_TOOL`; `ToolOutputError` carries `INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:487-515)
`ToolRunContext.deferContext()` queues context on the execution and the loop appends it only after the `tool/result` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:397-414)

mechanisms.name: tool-presentation-modes-and-ptc-collapse
mechanisms.what: One registry serves three presentation modes — `native`, `ptc`, `both` (`Config.mode`, default `native`) — resolved per scope by `modeFor()` with nearest-layer-wins, and overridable per agent by `tools.presentAs(mode)`, which additionally registers scope-local `tools:ptc-only` and `tools:sdk` prompt sections. Under `ptc` the model sees only `run_code` plus a generated SDK section (`renderToolsSdk` for TypeScript, `renderToolsSdkPy` for Python), and the SAME predicate (`collapses`) denies a model-direct call naming any other tool with `UNKNOWN_TOOL` plus a route hint, while a nested sub-dispatch (a `parent` token set) may call any visible tool. `run_code` is a stateless transport built lazily by `createRunCodeTool`; its `description` and `parameters` are lazy getters that resolve the mounted runtime's language flavor at schema-emission time, and a non-native mode with no `ctx.codeRuntime`, or a runtime whose `language` has no registered renderer, fails prompt assembly loudly.
invariants: The prompt rule and the executor denial share ONE predicate, so the prompt can never state a rule the registry does not enforce (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:847-855, 1314-1316).

`run_code` is reserved presentation infrastructure: never in the global layer, never shadowable, never restrictable, and invalid in `toolOrder` under `ptc` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:905-925, 1075-1077).
`both` renders the collapse section empty, because native calls do execute there so the rule would be false (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:844).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an absent code runtime or an unknown runtime language throws at prompt-assembly time; a model-direct call to a non-`run_code` tool under `ptc` becomes an `isError` `UNKNOWN_TOOL` result carrying the route hint.
constants: `mode` schema: union of 'native' | 'ptc' | 'both', default 'native' (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:784)
`maxParallelSubCalls` default 10 is the `run_code` program's overlap cap (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:660-666, 785, 921)
shipped SDK languages: 'typescript' and 'python' (packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:79-85)

mechanisms.name: parallel-tool-execution-with-commit-ordering
mechanisms.what: `executeToolCalls(ctx, turn, step, toolCalls, signal, acceptContext)` plans one assistant step's calls and partitions them by live `ctx.tools.executionMode`: a `parallel` first call takes the whole remaining group, anything else is a one-call exclusive barrier. Inside `runGroup`, `fillPool()` starts calls while `inFlight.size < maxParallelToolCalls` (default 10), and only the `dispatch` stage overlaps — ordered `prepare` (pre-execute plus guards) is awaited inside the lane before the next start. Results commit through a `commitReady()` cursor that advances only across CONTIGUOUS model-order slots, so `finalize`/`finish` (post-execute), the `tool/result` append and `additionalContexts` acceptance are strictly model-ordered even though tool bodies overlap; a later call whose live mode is no longer parallel breaks the pool and stays for the next barrier. The same submission-ordered contract is re-implemented inside `run_code` for nested sub-dispatches, with `maxParallelSubCalls` as the cap.
invariants: Ordered policy is never overlapped: only the around-dispatch/body stage runs concurrently, while pre-execute, post-execute and the durable appends stay in one ordered lane (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:86-89, 146-160, 216-218).

Dispatch overlaps, results do not: `commitReady()` stops at the first unset slot, so a slow early call blocks later commits but never later dispatch (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:147-160).

A scheduler failure drains started dispatches and rethrows WITHOUT fabricating tool results; only cancellation fabricates the ordered synthetic `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` results (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:113-121, 232-236).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — abort is fail-soft (started calls drain and commit, unstarted calls receive ordered synthetic `isError` results so replay stays valid); an internal scheduler failure is fail-closed (replenishment stops, already-started dispatches drain via `Promise.allSettled`, the first error is rethrown and no results are fabricated).
constants: `DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS` = 10 (packages/core/agent-loop/src/constants.ts:6)
adapter validation: `maxParallelToolCalls` must be a positive integer or config resolution throws (packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:191-195)
concurrency predicate `inFlight.size < maxParallelToolCalls` (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:200)
`run_code` sub-call cap `maxParallelSubCalls` default 10 (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:768-774, 921)

mechanisms.name: cooperative-cancellation-classification
mechanisms.what: Cancellation is caller-owned and cooperative: every `ToolExecutionInput` requires an `AbortSignal`, the registry keeps the original caller signal outside the wrapper-mutable execution object (`ToolCancellationState`), and after the around-dispatch wrappers run it re-fuses the caller signal with whatever replacement a wrapper installed (`fuseToolSignals`) so a replacement cannot detach caller cancellation. Which canonical failure wins depends solely on whether the body was invoked — `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` before, `ABORTED` after — and a started promise is never abandoned: it reaches quiescence before its outcome is replaced. The loop mirrors the split at the step boundary by appending synthetic `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` results, and `session-checkpoint-policy` consumes the same `tools/execute` seam to flush the session before a body runs and returns the same pre-dispatch abort result.
invariants: The registry re-fuses the original caller signal before the body, so an around-wrapper's signal replacement cannot detach caller cancellation (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:145-155, 1517-1533).
A started tool promise is never abandoned — it is awaited to quiescence and only its outcome is replaced (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:218-222, 226-239).
Caller cancellation replaces only a SUCCESSFUL accepted outcome; a tool-owned structured error survives it (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:156-166, 1580-1585).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — cancellation is fail-closed for the call (it becomes an `isError` result with a canonical code) but fail-soft for the pipeline (post-execute still runs and deferred context is preserved on the aborted result).
constants: `TOOL_ABORTED` = 'ABORTED' when the body was invoked, `TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` = 'ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH' when it was not (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:462-465, 1507-1515)
aborted result text 'Error: tool call aborted' / 'Error: tool call aborted before dispatch' (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1909-1934)
`info.name` is 'AbortError' for both canonical codes (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1916, 1930)

mechanisms.name: tool-call-timeout-policy
mechanisms.what: `ToolDefinition.timeoutMs` is a cooperative budget that is never sent to the model (`schemaOf` whitelists only name/description/parameters); the `timeout-policy` plugin wraps `tools/execute`, looks the definition up with `ctx.tools.get(exec.name, exec.agent)` and — only when a budget is declared — installs `using d = deadline(exec.signal, timeoutMs, TOOL_TIMEOUT)`, swaps `exec.signal` to the derived signal for the delegated dispatch, and restores the caller signal in `finally`. If and only if ITS OWN timer fired (`timeoutOf(d.signal, TOOL_TIMEOUT) !== undefined`, which distinguishes it from a nested outer deadline) the wrapper replaces whatever the tool returned with a structured `TOOL_TIMEOUT` error result. The shared `util/timeout` library owns `clampTimeout` (`min(requested ?? def, max)`), `deadline`, the rearmable `idleWatchdog` and `timeoutOf`; it only notifies through abort signals, so each capability still has to stop its own work.
invariants: Enforcement is cooperative: a tool that ignores `exec.signal` is awaited indefinitely, so declaring `timeoutMs` asserts the tool forwards the signal to an implementation that can reach quiescence (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:240-247).

Expiry is scoped by the plugin's own code, so a nested outer deadline reads as an ordinary upstream cancel rather than as this plugin's timeout (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:18-25, 69-75).
The caller's own signal is restored after dispatch so post-execute listeners never see the plugin's possibly-aborted timeout signal (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:61-66, 77-79).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — load/validation fails closed (`assertTimerDelay` rejects a non-positive, non-finite or over-cap delay) and the mapped expiry is fail-closed for the model (an `isError` `TOOL_TIMEOUT` result replaces the tool's own return), but a tool that never observes its signal is not forcibly stopped.
constants: `TOOL_TIMEOUT` = 'TOOL_TIMEOUT', used as both the deadline classification code and the structured error code (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:25)
`MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS` = 2_147_483_647 (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:25)
`timeoutMs <= 0` is the internal no-timer sentinel inside `deadline`, while public configs reject zero (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:45-55, 96-100)
search tools attach 30_000 ms; bash-local defaults 120_000 and caps at 600_000 (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:43; packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:107-108)

mechanisms.name: repeat-tool-call-reminder-guard
mechanisms.what: `repeat-tool-reminder` is an advisory per-agent consecutive-repeat detector registered as a `tools/post-execute` waterfall listener plus an `agent/pre-step` reset hook. It canonicalizes a call's arguments (deep key sort through `sortJsonValue` then `JSON.stringify`), keys a per-agent `WeakMap<Agent, Chain>` on `[name, canonical]`, and when the run length hits a configured threshold prepends a plugin-sourced `UserMessage` onto whatever the downstream decision was — including a `block` — through `additionalContexts`. It observes and enriches but never vetoes or rewrites: it counts FIRST, then delegates through `next()`. `include`/`exclude` are `*`-wildcard patterns compiled to anchored RegExps; untracked calls are transparent (neither count nor reset), and a user interjection deletes the chain.
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: counting happens before delegation and the reminder rides `additionalContexts` on both decision variants (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:209-224).

Counting lives in post-execute because denied calls flow through the same waterfall, and a model hammering a denied call is exactly the loop worth breaking (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:181-188).

The chain key always compares the FULL canonical string; `argumentsPreviewChars` bounds only the model-visible quote, never detection (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:35-42, 194-202).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed at plugin load (an empty `thresholds` list, a non-integer, a value below 2, a duplicate, or an `argumentsPreviewChars` below 1 all throw) and fail-open at runtime for the guarded call (it only prepends context and always calls `next()`).
constants: `thresholds` default `[3, 5, 8]` (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:46)
`argumentsPreviewChars` default 500, must be an integer >= 1 (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:49, 169-171)
every threshold must be an integer >= 2 with no duplicates (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:128-141)
the first threshold uses the gentle text, keyed to `thresholds[0]` rather than a literal count (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:59-67, 199-202)

mechanisms.name: output-spill-with-preview-and-locator
mechanisms.what: `spill-policy` prepends a `tools/post-execute` listener that first awaits `next()`, then applies, in order: the decision must be `accept`, must not replace `value`, the call must be top-level (`exec.parent === undefined`) and the tool must not be `read`; the resulting content must be all-text and its UTF-8 length must exceed `maxInlineBytes`. It then saves the FULL text through the optional `ctx.spillStore.saveText` (owner `{sessionId}`, source `{kind:'tool', toolName, callId, label}`) and replaces the model-facing content with a head/tail preview plus a formatted notice carrying the backend locator and retrieval hint. A second arm applies the same cap to `tools/ptc-dispatch-log`, so a `run_code` sub-call's durable log copy shrinks while the program's value stays complete. `LocalSpillStore` writes to `<root>/session-<sha256(sessionId)[0..12]>/<6-random-hex>-<encodedName>` with a `wx` create at mode 0o600 inside a 0o700 directory, and a best-effort activation sweep deletes spilled files older than `cleanupPeriodDays`.
invariants: The policy NEVER emits a replacement larger than the cap: the notice's worst-case byte cost is reserved INSIDE `maxInlineBytes` before the preview budget is computed, and when the notice alone exceeds the cap the inline content is kept (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:158-181).
A spill failure must NEVER turn a successful tool call into an `isError` or hide the inline result (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:33-35, 149-156).
A bad config must fail the deployment, not the tool: `maxInlineBytes` is validated at load, never per call (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:109-114).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft on every spill path (no owner session, no `ctx.spillStore`, a `saveText` rejection, or no within-cap replacement each log a warning through `ctx.logger.warn` and keep the original decision/content), fail-closed at load for an invalid `maxInlineBytes`; the store seam itself is fail-closed (it rejects on a real storage failure and leaves degradation to the caller).
constants: omitted `maxInlineBytes` means the plugin registers nothing at all (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:105-108); the shipped base profile sets 50000 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:386)
preview split: `headBytes = Math.ceil(budget/2)`, `tailBytes = Math.floor(budget/2)` (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:96-99)
notice reserve = `Buffer.byteLength(notice, 'utf8') + 2` and `previewBudget = Math.max(0, cap - reserve)` (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:166-167)
spill file: `open(path, 'wx', 0o600)` inside `mkdir(..., { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })`, name = 6 random bytes hex + encoded suggested name (packages/spill/spill-local/src/store.ts:109-115)

`cleanupPeriodDays` default 30, `0` disables the sweep, and only files strictly older than the cutoff expire (packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:68, 96; packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:256)

mechanisms.name: bounded-output-retention
mechanisms.what: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-output-retention` is a deliberately dependency-light library (no `ctx`, no registration, no events) that owns only the mechanical question 'what did we keep, what did we omit?'. `ItemRetainer` bounds an ordered stream of logical units with the single v1 strategy `{ kind: 'head', maxItems }`, while `TextRetainer` bounds a byte-oriented stream with `head`/`tail`/`headTail` over one shared prefix/suffix accumulator, trimming a partial UTF-8 sequence at each cut ONLY when a real omitted gap exists and reporting omission against the bytes ACTUALLY returned. `describeOmitted`/`formatRetentionNotice` standardize the omission wording while the calling tool supplies the recovery sentence. Production importers include the spill policy, the terminal renderer, the search core, the jobs tool and the session-reference projection.
invariants: The library owns only retention mechanics: file grouping, line numbering, exit codes, provider error states and the model-facing prose stay in the tool (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:1-20).
`truncated` means 'the retainer omitted otherwise-available content because of a budget' and never 'the upstream was incomplete' (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:10-15).

With nothing omitted the head|tail split is artificial, so `finish()` decodes the contiguous whole; only a real gap makes each side a true UTF-8-trimmed cut (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:356-370).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on a malformed budget (`assertBudget` throws from the constructor for a negative or non-integer cap); the retainers never throw on content and never reject.
constants: v1 item strategy is head-only: `{ kind: 'head', maxItems }` (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:86-91)
UTF-8 boundary trim scans back at most 3 continuation bytes (max sequence is 4) (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:211-222)
`TextRetainer` holds at most `prefixCap + suffixCap + one chunk` in memory (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:243-245)
no global thresholds: every cap is caller-supplied

mechanisms.name: file-tool-suite-with-observation-policy
mechanisms.what: `tool-fs` registers the model-facing `read`, `write`, `edit` (and `read_image` when `attachments` is mounted) over the `ctx.fs` seam; `read` windows lines (`READ_LIMIT` 2000), caps a single line at 2000 characters and the selected lines at 50 KiB, and switches to `streamText` at 10 MiB. Mutations pass through the single-slot `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent` waterfalls, which `fs-observation-policy` occupies with a per-owner `WeakMap<session, Map<targetKey, FsObservation>>`: an unseen or confirmed-absent target yields `createIfAbsent`, a present one yields `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version, and an unseen EDIT is rejected with `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` before any read. `LocalFileSystem` enforces the intent inside a per-`targetKey` FIFO lock and publishes through a private synced staging file (0o700 directory, `'wx'` 0o600 temp, `handle.sync()`), using a hard-link no-clobber primitive for `createIfAbsent`. `present` is the delivery endpoint: it validates 1..`maxFiles` existing regular files inside an OPEN turn and appends a durable `deliverables/presented` event only for a non-error result.
invariants: Without the observation policy the tools retain the bare provider's unconditional mutation behavior; the gate occupies the single decision slot and does NOT call `next()` (packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/src/index.ts:2-5, 116-122).
`fs/observed` must stay synchronous and non-throwing, because emit does not await promises and successful mutations have already committed (packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/src/index.ts:124-129).

A stale edit must report `FS_STALE_VERSION`, not `FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND`/`FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT` against newer content, so the version guard runs BEFORE literal matching (packages/fs/fs-local/src/index.ts:238-241).
The backend `cwd` is a resolution default, not a containment boundary (packages/fs/fs-local/src/index.ts:60-63).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — guarded mutations are fail-closed (a version mismatch, an unobserved edit and a blind overwrite each throw a coded `FsError`), `present` validation is fail-closed (non-existent or non-regular file, no open turn, over-cap file count all throw) while its durable event is fail-soft (skipped when the result is an error), and read truncation is fail-soft data on the result.
constants: `READ_LIMIT` 2000 lines, `READ_MAX_LINE_LENGTH` 2000 chars, `READ_MAX_BYTES` 50 * 1024, `STREAM_MIN_SIZE` 10 * 1024 * 1024 (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/read.ts:15, 21; packages/fs/tool-fs/src/read-render.ts:11, 14)
diff hunk context `DIFF_CONTEXT` = 3 (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/diff.ts:11)
`present` `maxFiles` default 8, accepted range 1..maxFiles per call (packages/fs/tool-present/src/index.ts:22, 79)
staging: directory mode 0o700, temp file `<basename>.tmp` opened `'wx'` 0o600, `handle.sync()` before publication (packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:599, 603, 609)
`createIfAbsent` publishes with `link()` (no-replace) and maps a collision to `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` (packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts:536-551, 567)

mechanisms.name: string-replace-patch-editing
mechanisms.what: `str_replace_editor` is an alternative single editor tool offering `view`, `create`, `str_replace` and `insert` over `ctx.fs`. `create` refuses an existing file and dispatches `fs/write-intent` defaulting to `{kind:'createIfAbsent'}`; `str_replace` requires a non-empty `old_str` and a non-null `new_str`, dispatches `fs/edit-intent`, reads the file, requires EXACTLY one literal occurrence (`FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND` when absent, `FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT` carrying the offending line numbers when not unique) and writes `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version; `insert` validates `0 <= insert_line <= lines.length`. Paths must be ABSOLUTE, `view` renders `cat -n`-style numbered lines or a listing two levels deep that hides dotfiles, `node_modules` and `__pycache__`, and every result is clipped at `maxOutputChars` with the literal `<response clipped>` note. Its `MutationPolicy` mirrors the tool-fs escalation split and maps `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` to the shared denial marker.
invariants: `old_str` must match a unique run of lines; a non-unique match is refused rather than guessed (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:27-30, 304-310).
A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted, but required parameters still need values (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:25, 283-285).
A long `view` result is truncated and explicitly marked with `<response clipped>` (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:24, 33-37).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a relative path, an existing `create` target, a missing or ambiguous match, a stale version and a sandbox denial each throw; only over-long output degrades (fail-soft) into a clipped result.
constants: `maxOutputChars` default 16_000 and must be a positive safe integer (packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor/src/index.ts:514, 524-525)

mechanisms.name: filesystem-and-shell-sandboxing
mechanisms.what: Confinement is a per-call policy check in trusted code over model-controlled input, not a kernel boundary. `SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem` fences ONLY `writeText`/`editText`: `checkedTarget` returns the target unfenced for `danger-full-access`, throws `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` for `read-only`, and for `workspace-write` RE-canonicalizes the path, requires it under a root of `writableRoots(policy)` and returns the FRESH target so the checked identity is the mutated one. `SandboxBashExecutor`/`SandboxPwshExecutor` subclass their local executors, stamp `sandboxPolicy: request.sandboxPolicy ?? ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()`, and wrap the exact local argv through `ctx.sandbox.confine(...)` for any non-full-access mode. On the tool side `FsSandboxController` advertises the `sandbox_permissions`/`justification` fields ONLY under a confining backend, so the schema validator rejects them otherwise, and it delegates the escalation approval sequence to the shared `dsh-sandbox` vocabulary so bash and fs escalate identically.
invariants: The fence narrows the symlink TOCTOU only by re-canonicalizing immediately before delegating, and containment is explicitly not a security boundary: kernel-grade isolation of untrusted CODE stays `ctx.shell`'s job (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:10-18, 129-143).
The fence must return the EXACT target the mutation will use, so no check-here-write-there window opens (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:111-114).
Escalation fields are advertised only under a confining backend, and a confining backend without `ctx.sandboxPolicy` throws at plugin load (packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:45-49, 59-65).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — a denial is reported as data in the sandbox shell path (`sandbox.denied`) while a taken escalation is fail-closed (approval must return a grant); a positively identified runner failure throws `SandboxUnavailableError` in the foreground and stamps `runnerFailed` on a background handle; `danger-full-access` runs unconfined by explicit opt-in.
constants: three handled modes 'danger-full-access', 'read-only', 'workspace-write', with both denials carrying `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED` (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts:122-143)

containment fallback compares `dev`+`ino` identity with `MISSING_CODES = {ENOENT, ENOTDIR}` and case-sensitivity default `process.platform !== 'win32'` (packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/containment.ts:12, 42-44, 61)

mechanisms.name: search-tools-and-native-command-resolution
mechanisms.what: `glob` and `grep` run the packaged ripgrep binary as an ordinary foreground `ctx.subprocess.spawn` with a plain argv vector — never `ctx.shell`, never a background job — with `--no-config` prepended so a host `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` cannot inject a `--pre` preprocessor. `grep` uses a fixed line-oriented `rg --json` command (path/line/text parse without colon ambiguity), treats exit 1 as zero results, and fails with `SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW` rather than parsing a partial stream; `glob` uses `rg --files --sort=modified` with two negated globs per VCS directory name and the search root behind `--` so a leading-dash path is never a flag. One retention pass bounds what survives inline, a separate pass bounds the serialized `presentationMeta`, and a `tools/post-execute` hook that fires only on an accepted, unmodified, direct top-level call saves the COMPLETE formatted result through `ctx.spillStore` and re-renders with the locator. `runNativeCommand` is the separate host-OS boundary: `execFile(command, args, { encoding: 'utf8', signal, windowsHide: true })` with no shell, carrying `code`/`stdout`/`stderr` on failure.
invariants: The search tools never use `ctx.shell` and never start a model-visible background task (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/index.ts:7-11).

A truncated result means complete stdout could not be retained within the budget, so the tool fails clearly instead of parsing a silently partial stream (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:132-137).
Native implementations never invoke a shell (packages/util/native-command/src/runner.ts:8).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — ripgrep acquisition is fail-closed (missing executable, raw-output overflow, invalid pattern and abort each throw a coded `SearchError`); retention and spill are fail-soft (a missing store or a rejected save only logs a warning and the footer states the remainder was not saved, so a successful search never becomes `isError`); `runNativeCommand` is fail-closed with no fallback path.
constants: `RAW_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` 20_000_000; `SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS` 30_000 (attached as `ToolDefinition.timeoutMs`); `SEARCH_STDERR_MAX_BYTES` 64 * 1024; `SEARCH_GRACE_MS` 3_000; `SEARCH_META_MAX_BYTES` 65_536 (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:36, 43, 50, 53, 65)
`GLOB_MAX_RESULTS` 100; `GLOB_VCS_EXCLUDES` = ['.git','.svn','.hg','.bzr','.jj','.sl'] with two negated globs each (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/glob.ts:25, 37, 100-103)
`GREP_MAX_MATCHES` 250; `GREP_MAX_LINE_BYTES` 2000; non-UTF-8 matched lines become '(line is not valid UTF-8)' (packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/grep.ts:29, 35, 157)

mechanisms.name: workspace-resolution-and-file-apis
mechanisms.what: `workspace/workspace` owns the durable workspace registry: `realpathNormalize` requires a fully qualified path before `realpath` and is the ONE uniqueness canon (string equality of canonicalized paths, so a symlink to an existing workspace's directory collides), `WorkspaceRegistry` writes through a versioned storage domain with a durable `pendingMutation` marker replayed before every serialized operation and rolled back on failure, and session membership requires BOTH an id in the record's account AND a session header whose canonical cwd equals the workspace path (filtered on read, never stored filtered). `api/workspace-files` exposes read-only Remote methods over `ctx.fs` with host-side page defaults (`maxBytes` 2 MiB, `maxFileBytes` 32 MiB, `maxLines` 5000, `maxEntries` 2000), a `workspaceFileScope` TypertLookup mapping a session id to its workspace root, lstat-before-resolve symlink rejection, and containment enforced only for `list`. `api/workspace-controller` owns the `workspace` Remote namespace and serializes every mutation on its own tail so title-ownership checks cannot interleave.
invariants: Workspace paths are stored canonicalized and uniqueness is string equality of canonicalized paths — a symlink to an existing workspace's directory collides (packages/workspace/workspace/src/paths.ts:41-44).

Membership requires both an id in the account and a session header whose canonical cwd equals the workspace path (packages/workspace/workspace/src/types.ts:26-29; packages/workspace/workspace/src/entity.ts:101-113).

Directory listings and change observations remain workspace-scoped while file reads follow the composed filesystem's read access, and this service exposes no mutations (packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:6-11).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — stored-state validation fails loud on a repeated id, an orphan record, a duplicate canonical path or a session accounted twice; a non-fully-qualified path is a `TypeError`; an out-of-workspace `list` is `workspace-file/outside-workspace` and a bad parameter is `gateway/bad-request`.
constants: `WorkspaceFiles` defaults `maxBytes` 2 * 1024 * 1024, `maxFileBytes` 32 * 1024 * 1024, `maxLines` 5000, `maxEntries` 2000 (packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:186-189)

storage domain name 'workspace' version 2, initial state `{ initialized: false, workspaceIds: [], archivedSessionIds: [] }`, `pendingMutation` a union of exactly 'create' | 'delete' (packages/workspace/workspace/src/spec.ts:38-41, 69-73)
`readAll` checks `info.size > limit` and then reads `limit + 1` bytes to detect overflow (packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts:281, 284)

error codes `workspace/invalid-path`, `workspace/name-conflict`, `workspace/move-invalid`, `workspace/not-found`, `session/not-found` (packages/api/workspace-controller/src/commands.ts:51, 76, 133, 158, 178)

mechanisms.name: atomic-write-and-cross-process-locking
mechanisms.what: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write` provides `writeFileAtomic(filename, content, { mode, dirMode? })`: create parents, write a random-suffix sibling `${filename}.<12 hex>.tmp` with flag `'wx'` and the caller's mode, then rename it over the target, so readers observe either the old or the new complete content and a replaced file ends up with exactly the stated mode; transient Windows `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` renames are retried with exponential backoff. `withFileLock(filename, operation, { waitMs? })` serializes cross-process writers through a `wx`-created `<filename>.lock` sibling holding the pid, backing off exponentially and failing on a deadline, while readers stay lock-free because the rename commit is atomic. A SECOND and different `writeFileAtomic` lives in `fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts`: it fsyncs the staging file, preserves the Windows DACL and publishes `createIfAbsent` through a hard link.
invariants: The temp open refuses to follow a symlink planted at the temp path, the fresh inode carries `options.mode` through the rename (no chmod race), and the rename replaces a symlinked target itself instead of writing through to its referent (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:64-73).
A contender never removes an existing lock because file age cannot prove its owner stopped; orphan recovery is an operator action (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:147-151).
Crash durability (fsync) is explicitly out of scope for this package (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:73; TODO at :83-84).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — any remaining rename failure removes the temp file and rethrows; lock contention outliving the deadline throws a timed-out error; a non-contention error propagates unchanged.
constants: `WINDOWS_TRANSIENT_RENAME_ERRORS` = {EACCES, EBUSY, EPERM}; retry 20 ms initial, doubling to a 200 ms cap, at most 8 retries (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:17-20)
`DEFAULT_LOCK_WAIT_MS` = 2_000; lock retry 20 ms initial with a 200 ms cap (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:114-115, 126)
lock file `<filename>.lock` with content `${process.pid}` newline, mode 0o600, flag 'wx' (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:162, 167)
random temp suffix `randomBytes(6).toString('hex')` = 12 hex chars; `mode` is REQUIRED in `WriteFileAtomicOptions` (packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:53, 85)

mechanisms.name: shell-tools-and-persistent-sessions
mechanisms.what: `ctx.shell` is an abstract `ShellExecutor` seam (resolve, then run/start), implemented by `bash-local` and `pwsh-local`, which fill and clamp a request into a spec (`clampTimeout(request.timeoutMs, config.timeoutMs, config.maxTimeoutMs)` and `stdoutMaxBytes` from `config.maxOutputBytes`), open ONE fused deadline per foreground run (`deadline(spec.signal, spec.timeoutMs, 'BASH_TIMEOUT')`) and classify the outcome as `timedOut = timeoutOf(d.signal, code) !== undefined` versus `aborted = d.signal.aborted && !timedOut`, so a timeout and an abort racing before process close report the single first cause. Collect-mode readers cap in-memory output and spill overflow to a capped temp file; the renderers append a stable exit contract (`[timed out after Nms]`, `[killed by signal: X]`, `[exit code: N]`) that `parseExitStatus` inverts to drive the terminal card's exit pill. The persistent variants keep ONE PTY session per agent through `ctx.terminals`, wrap each command in nonce start/end markers and serialize commands per owner on a promise chain; they do NOT go through `ctx.shell`, so executor config (timeout, grace, sandbox mode) does not apply to them.
invariants: `run()` rejects only for infrastructure failures: nonzero exits, timeout kills and abort kills resolve with a `ShellRunResult` (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:51-53).
A still-running background process is stopped and awaited when its owning composition tears down, so a background process survives an executor-only reload (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:59-62).

Keep the persistent wrapper on ONE physical line: an interactive bash prints PS2 for embedded newlines before executing the buffer, which would leak terminal prompts and marker source text into the model-facing result (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:81-83).
The exit marker must stay last because `parseExitStatus` anchors there (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/render.ts:44).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-soft at run time (a timeout, an abort or a nonzero exit is data on the result; a background handle's `done` never rejects and a provider rejection settles as `killed` with the detail on stderr) and fail-closed at resolve/load time (a non-positive or non-finite timeout, a `graceMs` above the timer cap, or a confining executor without `ctx.sandboxPolicy` throws).
constants: `bash-local` defaults: `timeoutMs` 120_000, `maxTimeoutMs` 600_000, `maxOutputBytes` 64_000, `maxSpillBytes` 64 MiB, `graceMs` 3_000 (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:34-38, 105-112)
`ENV_OVERRIDES` = { NO_COLOR: '1', TERM: 'dumb', PAGER: 'cat', GIT_PAGER: 'cat' } (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:27-32)

persistent bash/pwsh default `timeoutMs` 300_000 and `maxOutputChars` 16_000, with `SCROLLBACK_PAGE_LINES` 1_000 and `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` 25 (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:24-25, 449-450; packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:486-487)
`clampTimeout` = `Math.min(requested ?? def, max)` and rejects a non-positive or non-finite hint (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:45-55)

mechanisms.name: pty-terminal-sessions
mechanisms.what: `terminal/terminal` is an in-process `TerminalSessionService` at `ctx.terminals` holding a backend registry, exact-Agent sessions, reserved names, pending spawns and owner cleanups with a memoized `disposeAll`. `terminal-bash` supplies the default backend: a headless terminal emulator plus a `BoundedTextBuffer` scrollback, a sanitizer driven by the prompt marker `133;D;` and the controlled prompt `dsh> `, and a settled-operation protocol with wait reasons (idle silence, handoff grace, timeout, exit). The real PTY is allocated by `subprocess-local`'s `spawnTerminal` through `node-pty` with `{name:'dumb', rows, cols, cwd, env}`, and `tool-terminal` registers the model-facing `terminal_open`/`terminal_send`/`terminal_read`/`terminal_signal`/`terminal_close`/`terminal_list` tools with a complete-result byte cap. Unix stdin-wait detection reads `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/syscall` (including fd-0 inspection for select/poll/epoll) to prove a foreground group is actually blocked reading the terminal; Windows hard-codes false and delivers Ctrl-C as a `\x03` write.
invariants: Whole-session quiescence is the seam contract: `spawnTerminal` owns terminal allocation, text transport, foreground groups, signalling and an awaited termination method (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:109-113).
Already-adopted members keep their own start identities, which every signal rechecks (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/terminal.ts:200).

Local PTY allocation is synchronous but the provider contract permits remote asynchronous allocation; a first genuinely asynchronous step in a handle call must add the operation tracking a remote provider needs (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/index.ts:229-230; packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/terminal.ts:51-55).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed for allocation and teardown (a missing program, an already-aborted signal or an `node-pty.spawn` throw rejects `spawnTerminal`; teardown throws when descendants or the shell survive the SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL ladder; a write after exit throws); fail-open for stdin-wait detection, where every read failure returns false and readiness degrades to 'not waiting'.
constants: `terminal-bash` defaults: rows 40, cols 160, `scrollbackLines` 10_000, `scrollbackMaxBytes` 4 MiB, `maxReadBytes` 256 KiB, `pollIntervalMs` 50, `exactProbeAfterMs` 150, `idleSilenceMs` 3_000, `handoffGraceMs` 500, `timeoutMs` 30_000, `disposeGraceMs` 3_000, with `maxReadBytes <= scrollbackMaxBytes` enforced (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:89-99, 116-117)
`DEFAULT_BASH_SHELL` '/bin/bash'; `DEFAULT_BASH_ARGS` ['--noprofile','--norc','-i']; `DEFAULT_PWSH_ARGS` ['-NoLogo','-NoProfile'] (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:54-58)
`PROMPT_MARKER_PREFIX` '133;D;' and `CONTROLLED_PROMPT` 'dsh> ' (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/sanitize.ts:6, 9)
`tool-terminal`: `DEFAULT_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` 256 * 1024, `MIN_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` 64, `enableRunInBackground` default true (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts:29-46)

mechanisms.name: subprocess-spawn-and-process-tree-control
mechanisms.what: `SubprocessRuntime` is the abstract `ctx.subprocess` seam with `resolveExecutable`/`spawn`/`spawnTerminal`, and `subprocess-local` implements it: it scrubs credential-shaped and all `DSH_*` environment names from every child, validates argv/cwd/env for NUL bytes, resolves executables against the scrubbed PATH (reimplementing libuv's Windows search order) and owns each managed range through a selected containment mode. `selectContainmentMode` prefers a Linux user-systemd transient scope, then a Win32 Job Object for ordinary spawns, and otherwise degrades to a detached process-group/`taskkill` fallback with exactly one warning. Termination is one ladder: a one-shot `terminateWithReason` sends SIGTERM on the platform owner and arms `setTimeout(kill('SIGKILL'), graceMs)`, the spec's abort signal is wired through the same entry, and collection keeps the last `maxBytes` in memory while spilling the head to a capped temp file. `win32-process` supplies the koffi FFI layer: a kill-on-close Job created through `CreateJobObjectW`, with membership established by creating the process `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assigning it to the Job and then resuming the thread.
invariants: The seam applies no defaults: every disposition, limit and directory is explicit, so the caller's own config decides them (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts:69-74).
Credential-shaped names are NOT forwarded implicitly; a deliberately supplied entry survives because explicit env layers merge after the scrub (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:38-45).
The grace timer is deliberately NOT cleared on settlement: forced termination must still reach range survivors (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:611-612).
A Job member can never escape unowned: every failure after creation terminates the just-created process and closes the Job before throwing (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:434-478).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — spawn validation is fail-closed (an already-aborted signal, an empty `argv[0]`, an invalid grace or a NUL byte throws before launch, and a runner start/protocol failure is an infrastructure error); signalling delivery is fail-soft (failures are swallowed so teardown stays idempotent) and output overflow is fail-soft (the tail is retained, `lossy`/`truncated` is set, and the spill path is advertised when intact).
constants: `SENSITIVE_ENV_PATTERN` = /KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i and the scrub also drops every `DSH_*` name (packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:45, 64-68)
spill: `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-subprocess-'))` at 0700 and a file created `'wx'` 0o600 with a 6-byte-hex suffix (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts:97-99, 193-205)

Job limits: `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` 0x00002000 at flags offset 16 of a 144-byte `JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_SIZE`, `JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation` class 9, `ActiveProcesses` read at offset 40 of a 48-byte accounting buffer, `STARTUPINFOW` size 104 with `STARTF_USESTDHANDLES`, `CREATE_SUSPENDED` 0x4 plus `CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` 0x400, `HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT` 0x1 (packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/abi.ts:4-48; packages/subprocess/win32-process/src/process.ts:400-426)
win32 Job-emptiness poll cadence 10 ms (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/windows-job.ts:163-189)

mechanisms.name: code-runtime-isolation
mechanisms.what: `ctx.codeRuntime` is an abstract `CodeRuntime` seam (`language`, `isolation`, `run(request)`) owning the cross-backend portability vocabulary (`RESERVED_BINDING_GLOBALS`, `RESERVED_ERROR_MEMBERS`, `DUNDER_MEMBER`, `PORTABLE_RESERVED_WORDS`) and an error-as-field contract: program, budget, abort and substrate failures resolve inside `CodeRunResult`, while Service Definition misuse rejects. The shipped backend is `WorkerThreadCodeRuntime` (typescript, worker-thread): it type-strips the program with `stripTypeScriptTypes`, spawns a `Worker` with `env: {}`, `execArgv: []`, `stdout`/`stderr` enabled and `resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb`, races the settle paths (done frame, output limit, ELU-poll compute budget, wall timer, abort listener, worker error/exit), re-validates and rebuilds every inbound port message field by field because the peer runs model code, and accounts combined logs plus value bytes with a hand-written JSON byte ledger that captures intrinsics so model-mutated prototypes cannot alter accounting. The private `experimental/code-runtime-python` backend runs CPython in its own process group with RLIMIT_CPU/RLIMIT_AS, an fd-3 JSON-lines protocol, SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL escalation and a PID-reuse guard comparing `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22.
invariants: The peer runs model code, so every inbound message is re-validated and rebuilt and junk is dropped rather than thrown, because a throw in the host's `message` listener would crash the host (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:136-139, 509-512).
Executable logic stays in `bootstrap.ts` for in-process coverage, while `worker.ts` is the spawn-only entrypoint (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/worker.ts:2-3).

The Python backend is containment, not a security boundary: model code has bash-equivalent trust, contained by a tempdir-only environment, resource limits, a wall timeout and process-group kill escalation (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:4-6).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — Service Definition misuse and invalid configuration fail closed (throwing at load or from `run()`), while everything a program or the substrate can cause (exception, invalid-output, output-limit, timeout, abort, worker-exit) resolves as `result.error`; hostile port traffic is dropped silently; crossing the output ledger converts the run into an explicit `output-limit` failure rather than a silently truncated success.
constants: worker-thread defaults: `computeMs` 60_000, `maxWallMs` 600_000, `maxOutputBytes` 67_108_864 (64 MiB), `maxOldGenerationSizeMb` 512 (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:239-243)

`ELU_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` 25; `MIN_OUTPUT_BYTES` 4; the ledger starts at 2 bytes with +1 separator byte per extra log entry (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:63, 66, 170, 177)

python defaults: `cpuSeconds` 60, `maxWallMs` 600_000, `addressSpaceMb` 512, `maxLogBytes` 65_536, `maxValueBytes` 32_768, `graceMs` 3_000, `pythonBin` 'python3'; `PROTOCOL_FD` 3; `MIN_CPYTHON` {3,10}; `PYTHON_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` 5_000; `FRAME_PARSE_CAP_BYTES` 64 MiB (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:212, 497, 500, 806-814; packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/protocol.ts:18)

`code-runtime-python` is `"private": true` and loaded by no shipped bundle, only by a snapshot profile (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/package.json:41; snapshots/session/ptc-python-turn/cordis.yml:29-30)

mechanisms.name: e2b-remote-execution-backends
mechanisms.what: Three E2B packages implement the same seams against a remote sandbox instead of the host. `e2b/e2b` registers `ctx.e2b` as the single shared sandbox owner (`Sandbox.create({ apiKey, timeoutMs, secure: true, lifecycle: { onTimeout: 'kill' } })`, a fresh randomized HOME for control commands, `chmod 700` on `<cwd>/.dsh-e2b`, kill-and-rethrow on setup failure). `e2b/fs-e2b` implements `FileSystem` by running canonicalization inside the sandbox (`realpath -mz | base64`), sampling the first 8192 bytes for binary detection, and publishing writes through a private 0700 staging directory plus `rename` or a guarded `ln -T` create. `e2b/subprocess-e2b` implements `SubprocessRuntime` by resolving executables with `command -v` inside the sandbox, validating argv/cwd/env for NUL bytes, and polling remote status at a configurable cadence. In-tree, `e2b/e2b` and `e2b/fs-e2b` are referenced only by their own test-fixture composition and no shipped bundle mounts any of the three.
invariants: Each handle starts through the SHARED sandbox and retains command output/status paths in that remote world (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:1-5).

The remote grace bound mirrors `subprocess-local`'s spawn-time check, because an unbounded grace would make the remote force-escalation deadline unreachable (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:40-50).
A remote write must not be readable by other local users and must not be redirectable through a planted symlink (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:30-32, 556-584).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — `E2BRuntime.validate()` throws on an empty API key, a non-absolute Linux cwd or a non-positive `timeoutMs`; a setup failure kills the sandbox and rethrows; the fs provider throws coded `FsError`s and removes its staging directory on a failed write; `E2BSubprocessRuntime.spawn` throws before launch for a disposing service, an empty `argv[0]`, an unrepresentable grace or an already-aborted signal.
constants: `e2b`: cwd default '/home/user/workspace', `timeoutMs` default 300_000, control HOME `/.dsh-e2b-control-<uuid>`, runtime root `<cwd>/.dsh-e2b` chmod 700 (packages/e2b/e2b/src/index.ts:41, 80-81, 105, 175)
`subprocess-e2b`: `pollMs` default 20 (packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b/src/index.ts:63-65)
`fs-e2b`: `BINARY_SAMPLE_BYTES` 8192; staging directory `.dsh-<uuid>.tmp` at 0o700; new files 0o600 while existing files keep `mode & 0o777` (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:31, 567, 574, 581-584)
